description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join the founding engineering team building an AI agent framework for farm operations. You will design and ship systems that help agents handle real business decisions, with direct feedback from the teams using them.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and own the agent framework, including roles, tools, permissions, approvals, and runtime orchestration for long-running tasks.

 - Build memory and context systems that give agents relevant farm-specific knowledge, including operational knowledge that may not be documented.

 - Develop code automation that supports repeatable work and escalates unexpected situations to human oversight.

 - Create evaluations and safety measures to build trust and track agent performance over time.

 - Build tools on top of the data layer and integrate machine learning insights into the framework.

 - Work with farm teams to observe real-world usage and improve the product based on feedback.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Two to four years of engineering experience shipping production LLM agents or agentic workflows that people rely on.

 - Experience building agents with tool use, context and memory design, orchestration, and evaluation.

 - Strong Python skills and familiarity with PostgreSQL, asynchronous systems, and workflow engines.

 - Experience writing evaluations, investigating real-world user needs, and independently performing system design and critically reviewing AI-generated code.

 - Knowledge of memory, retrieval, and context management, including when work should be handed to a person or handled with conventional code.

 - Experience with durable workflow engines such as Temporal, agent observability and tracing, or security topics such as prompt injection and permissions is a plus.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary is $170,000 to $200,000 annually, plus 1% equity with four-year vesting and a one-year cliff. Benefits include healthcare, AI coding tools and model access, and work hardware. Visa sponsorship is not available; candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, five days a week, with about one week of travel per quarter to farms in Washington, Oregon, and California.
